text:
The Islanders arrive at Nashville after a 6-3 loss at Dallas, where the Stars extended their winning streak to five. They're 2-1-2 in their last five and are without Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie, so Simon Holmstrom has moved onto the first power-play unit and is up to 19:59 a night from 15:43. The Predators are also 2-1-2 over five, but they're coming off a 6-2 win over Colorado.

On chance creation, our model has this close: 2.98 expected goals (the quality of shots, not just the count) for NYI tonight and 3.04 for NSH. New York has controlled more of the play at five on five (49% of expected goals to Nashville's 43%), though it takes 4.5 penalties a game. The penalty kill favors Nashville, which allows 0.53 expected goals per game shorthanded against the Islanders' 0.89. In net, Semyon Varlamov (projected) is at +4.3 goals saved above expected, meaning goals prevented beyond what the shots called for, across three games. Juuse Saros (projected) is at +2.9 this season after finishing last year at -10.2 over 59 games.

Watch Bo Horvat, whom we have at 39% to score, and Matthew Schaefer, on a four-game point streak. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos is at 36% and Filip Forsberg at 32%. Our under-the-radar pick is Matthew Wood, a fourth-liner at about 13:28 a night whose shots have been dangerous: 2.8 expected goals in his last 10 games. We have him at 19% to score, a player to watch, nothing more.
